metadata.research_title: Electric vehicle awareness and perceived adoption barriers in Kerala
metadata.subtitle: An exploratory analysis of a 2021 survey
metadata.institution: Department of Economics, Union Christian College Aluva; affiliated to Mahatma Gandhi University Kottayam
metadata.source_pdf_filename: AWARENESS OF ELECTRIC VEHICLES AND THEIR POPULARITY IN KERALA.pdf
metadata.provenance: Rewritten and reanalysed from the published aggregate tables of the original BA project. No raw survey responses were available. Reported counts were retained; percentages and interpretations were corrected.
metadata.copyright_or_reuse_license: No public reuse license has been specified. Do not invent a Creative Commons license.

charts.title: Reported awareness in the survey sample
charts.source: Source: Original survey report (2021), Tables 4.2.1, 4.3.2 and 4.4.4, pp. 48, 55 and 69. Counts retained; percentages recalculated.
charts.note: Self-reported awareness, not a validated knowledge score. Each percentage uses its stated group denominator.

charts.title: Perceived barriers among respondents
charts.source: Source: Original survey report (2021), Tables 4.2.4, 4.3.11 and 4.4.7, pp. 52, 63-64 and 74. Counts retained; percentages recalculated. Multiple responses permitted. Percentages are shares of respondents and need not sum to 100%. The unreported other category is excluded.
charts.note: Multiple answers permitted; percentages use 400 respondents, not 875 reported selections. Percentages need not sum to 100. The other category was offered but not tabulated.

charts.title: Professionals answering yes to purchase consideration

data.label: Rapid public charging within five kilometres plus home charging

charts.source: Source: Original survey report (2021), Table 4.4.5, pp. 71-72. Counts retained; percentages recalculated. Denominator 101 for each question. Nearby means within a five-kilometre radius in the questionnaire. The scenarios are separate questions, not randomised treatments.
charts.note: Separate hypothetical questions to 101 professionals. Aggregate margins cannot show individual changes. These are not causal effects, actual sales or estimates of willingness to pay.
